solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Long Island is shelter for grass house

definitions.note: adjective here, as in a marathon session; the answer is usually a noun

indicators.note: something that shelters another holds it inside, so the island word wraps round what follows

blocks.note: the Isle of Man
to grass is to inform on someone, as a rat does
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A home on Long Island built to keep out the weather, perhaps with a lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long Island' reads as the New York place, but the clue splits after 'Long'. The Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon meeting or session is an extremely lengthy, drawn-out one, so the word works as an adjective meaning protracted.

clue.text: Lying in state, English seeker of justice

indicators.note: a thing lying in something rests inside it, so the English abbreviation sits within the word for state

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
a common abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English campaigner for justice lies in state after death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying in state' reads as a funeral ritual, but 'Lying in' is the container signal and 'state' is a verb meaning assert.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger exacts retribution for a wrong, pursuing a kind of rough justice on behalf of the injured party.

clue.text: Tropical bird, a new one

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone spots a tropical bird and remarks that it is a new species to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The ani is a black cuckoo of the American tropics, a crosswordland favourite among short bird names.

clue.text: Take centre stage in talk show

blocks.note: first meaning: to speak at length and dominate a conversation
second meaning: an older sense, to offer or hold out for display

explanation.surface: A guest grabs the spotlight on a television chat programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk show' looks like a single phrase; the split comes between them, with 'show' standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds forth lectures everyone present, and in its older sense the phrase means to proffer or exhibit something.

clue.text: Even if smart, also into stupid things

indicators.note: stupid things are muddled, so the letters of things are jumbled
one thing goes into another, so the word for also is placed inside the jumble

blocks.note: someone smart is no twit
taken as written, to be rearranged
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A clever person can still enjoy silly pursuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' is read whimsically as 'no twit', a phrase for someone who is not foolish; the jumbled things then wrap round the word for also.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a conjunction, notwithstanding introduces a concession, much like although or despite the fact that.

clue.text: Dry peak area

blocks.note: sec describes dry wine
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A walker describes a parched summit region.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct part or zone of a larger whole, such as a district of a city or a battlefield.

clue.text: Baby—super-tough, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions only

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A baby that is remarkably hardy, in a strange way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a small child or infant, a jokey informal word for offspring.

clue.text: They can accommodate little piggies, bless them!

definitions.text: They can accommodate little piggies, bless them!

blocks.note: surface reading: a pen or sty for piglets
setter's reading: the little piggies are toes, as in the nursery rhyme, and the whole thing is the British endearment 'bless your ...'

explanation.walkthrough: 'This little piggy' is the toe-counting rhyme, so the piggies are toes; 'bless his cotton socks' is a fond British expression for a sweet child.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn on the feet hold the toes, and the phrase completes the affectionate idiom about blessing someone endearing.

clue.text: Service book from Ford in a library

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of Ford, the whole of in and a, and the start of library

explanation.surface: A prayer book borrowed from a library by someone called Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal is a book setting out the forms of church services, especially those for ordaining clergy.

clue.text: MP on trial, so worried

indicators.note: something worried is shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so these letters are disturbed

blocks.note: in cricket, the on side is also called the leg side
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician facing a court case is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' = LEG is a cricket convention: the half of the field behind a batter's legs is the leg or on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is a lawmaker, one of the people who draft and vote on new statutes.

clue.text: Performance unfinished?

blocks.note: first meaning: a fuss or commotion, as in 'what a performance!'
second meaning: still waiting to be done, as on a list of tasks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Performance' suggests a stage show, but here it is the fuss sense; the second definition is the hyphen-free 'to do' of a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a bustle or uproar, and a task still to do has not yet been completed.

clue.text: Old silver and lead regularly used

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Antique metals, silver and lead, routinely employed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead is also a metal (Pb), which tempts a symbol, but here the word itself supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged and old both describe someone or something having lived or existed for a long time.

clue.text: He did our son wrong, refused to pay

indicators.note: to do something wrong is to get it out of order, so these letters are set awry

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has wronged our son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' looks like a verb in the surface; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank that dishonours a cheque declines to honour it, so the payment is not made.

clue.text: OK, train rides are here

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun: the place where rides are

blocks.note: fair means acceptable, all right
to ground someone in a subject is to train them in its basics

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a train ride is available here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway vehicle, but it is the verb, as in 'well grounded in Latin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an open site holding a travelling funfair, with roundabouts, dodgems and other amusements.

clue.text: Before play, check sporting kit

blocks.note: surface reading: an athlete inspecting equipment ahead of a match
setter's reading: sporting means wearing, and the play is a theatrical one, so the kit is stage costume tried out before opening night

explanation.walkthrough: 'play' and 'sporting kit' suggest a game; the play is drama, and 'sporting' means wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The final run-through before a theatre opening is performed in full costume, checking the whole show as it will be seen.

clue.text: Pest spray can, anyone?

indicators.note: a spray scatters things widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an aerosol of insecticide to deal with a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pest spray' reads as one noun phrase; the definition is 'Pest' alone, and 'spray' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is a nuisance, a person or thing that irritates, which is exactly what an annoyance is.

clue.text: Waste taps to turn on and off?

blocks.note: to blow money is to waste it
the two taps on a basin

explanation.surface: Leaving the taps running wastes water, so turn them on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn on and off' sounds like operating taps; it means to keep changing one's attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow hot and cold is to vacillate, being enthusiastic one moment and indifferent the next.

clue.text: An attempt to throw up sausage

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
to have a go is to make an attempt
to lob is to throw in a high arc

explanation.surface: Someone tries to vomit up a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw up' reads as vomiting; 'throw' is LOB and 'up' turns the whole string over.
explanation.definitionFit: Bologna is a large smoked sausage named after the Italian city, known in America as baloney.

clue.text: Toilet paper alternative over in lounge

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair inside the word for lounge

blocks.note: to loll is to lounge lazily
or introduces an alternative
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A spare supply of toilet paper is kept in the sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, abbreviated O in scorebooks.
explanation.definitionFit: The two phrases are the same thing: a cylinder of tissue for use in a lavatory.

clue.text: Ice for this lolly

blocks.note: surface reading: a frozen ice lolly, a British name for an ice pop
setter's reading: ice is slang for kill and lolly is slang for cash, so this is payment for a murder

explanation.walkthrough: An ice lolly is the British name for a popsicle; split apart, 'ice' means kill and 'lolly' means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment made to a hired killer, or compensation paid to a victim's family, is cash tainted by a death.

clue.text: Substantial to consume, my sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between its outer slices, so the outer word encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to eat is to consume food

explanation.surface: My sandwiches are filling and hearty to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meaty has real substance or depth, like a weighty argument or a solid role.

clue.text: Son confused by girl’s first kiss

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their normal order
first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A boy is flustered by a girl giving him his first kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Snog is British slang for a long, passionate kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A snog is an informal British word for a kiss, especially a prolonged amorous one.

clue.text: Jelly derived from a fish

blocks.note: taken as written
the gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A jelly made from fish, like aspic or isinglass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gelatine from fish; the real source is seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance extracted from seaweed, used to set food and grow bacterial cultures.

clue.text: Misleading people leads to social detachment

blocks.note: a lie is something misleading
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Deceiving the public breeds isolation within society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misleading' looks like an adjective on 'people'; it stands for A LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is estrangement, the feeling of being isolated from or hostile to the surrounding community.

clue.text: Wife enters before couple

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so the wife abbreviation is put within the next word

blocks.note: as in 'ten to six', meaning before the hour
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: The wife walks in ahead of the rest of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, the number two in everyday speech.

clue.text: To west of railway, river also stopped flowing

indicators.note: in an across entry, west is the left, so the following pieces come before the railway abbreviation

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
and means also
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: West of the train line, a river has dried up as well.
explanation.definitionFit: When a supply runs dry its source has dried up, so nothing more comes out.

clue.text: US city, described by Great Britain, like empty French city

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the outer letters surround the city
an empty word has had its inside taken out, leaving only its outermost letters

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
Reno is a city in Nevada
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An American city compared by Britain to a deserted French one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' uses the geometry sense: a line drawn around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenoble is a city in south-eastern France, in the Alps, which hosted the 1968 Winter Olympics.
